transcript: let's talk about Amber Riley in Dreamgirls because yes I was lucky enough to see her play Effie in 2017 and now people are wondering if she will return for the upcoming Broadway revival welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history so even way before Amber Riley actually played the role in London a lot of people dreamcast her as Effie or kind of associated her with the role partly because it's just very intuitive dream casting but also because of her iconic performance of “and I'm telling you I'm not going” on Glee so for her to actually get cast in the role in real life was like this big dream come true event for Glee fans of course this was years before Lea Michele had her own similar full circle moment as Fanny Brice having said that it wasn't necessarily all it was cracked up to be the role is of course, very demanding and it seemed like Amber Riley struggled a bit with the show schedule I believe she had an alternate which makes total sense but on top of that I believe she had other absences she was out with pneumonia at one point which really sucks and even just anecdotally speaking I remember hearing a bunch of stories of people going to see her and getting her understudy on days when she was otherwise scheduled to perform and I don't mean any of that in a judgemental way toward her or the covers it's a tough role and it was a tough situation and as far as her performance itself some have said that her acting in the role was not necessarily on par with her singing in the role and I have to confess that I was kind of in that camp as well although I do think that what she did with the role ultimately worked partly because she's just such a ridiculously good vocalist that inevitably there's gonna be a lot of raw power and emotional expression that comes through from that alone but I also remember thinking that she came across very young on stage and of course she was technically older than both Jennifer Hudson and Jennifer Holliday when they played the role but still I remember her having this very youthful energy that made her come across as very vulnerable and sympathetic of course if she were to return to the role next year as some people are hoping for she would you know naturally not read as young on stage, of course but you know maybe she would have a little bit more comfort and ease in the text and scene work than she did when I saw her but I still thought overall it was a great performance and clearly she was doing something right cause she did win the Olivier Award for it and of course it has to be said that hearing her sing “and I'm telling you I'm not going” live was one of those great, rare moments in musical theatre that was so overwhelming that I felt like I had a physical reaction to it even from way up in the nosebleeds I remember my muscles tensed up my heart was beating faster and I just felt like I was witnessing something very special
